title: Split solver from a round contract
statement: Let $f,T_E:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $B$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $q$ be one of its states, and let $A\in\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every Boolean word $w$, the machine started on $w$ reaches the configuration at state $q$ with all work tapes blank within $A(T_E(|w|+1)+|w|+2)$ steps, and is not in state $q$ at any earlier step. Suppose also that for every $w$ and every candidate word $s$ with $|s|\le |w|+1$, there is a positive number of steps $t\le A(T_E(|w|+1)+|w|+2)$ such that the run from state $q$ on $w$ with $s$ on the first work tape and the other work tapes blank does not visit $q$ at any intermediate step strictly between steps $0$ and $t$. If $|s|+f(|s|)=|w|$, that run halts at step $t$ with output the self-delimiting encoding of the prefix of $w$ of length $|s|$ and the remaining suffix; otherwise it reaches state $q$ with the candidate updated by the split step. Then there are a finite-state Boolean Turing machine $M$ and a natural number $c$ such that, on every input $w$, $M$ outputs the encoding of the split of $w$ at the least $i\le |w|$ satisfying $i+f(i)=|w|$, or the empty word if no such $i$ exists, and halts after exactly $c(|w|+1)(T_E(|w|+1)+|w|+2)$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $f,T_E$ map natural numbers to natural numbers
$B$ is a finite-state Boolean Turing machine
For each input $w$, startup reaches the anchor configuration within the stated bound
The startup run avoids state $q$ at every earlier step
For each $w,s$ with $|s|\le |w|+1$, a round takes a positive number of steps no greater than the stated bound
A round avoids state $q$ strictly between its initial and final steps
When $|s|+f(|s|)=|w|$, the round halts with the encoded split at $|s|$
When the equality fails, the round returns to state $q$ with the stepped candidate
replaced:
Let a body machine with an anchor state satisfy a startup contract and a
round contract with common envelope $A\,(T_E(n+1) + n + 2)$, where the round
from a candidate $s$ of length at most $n+1$ either halts with the encoded
split of the input at $\abs{s}$ when $\abs{s} + f(\abs{s})$ equals the input
length, or returns to the anchor with the stepped candidate, never visiting
the anchor strictly inside. Then there exist a machine $M$ and a constant
$c$ computing, within $c\,(n+1)(T_E(n+1) + n + 2)$ steps, the function
sending $w$ to the pair encoding of the split of $w$ at the least $i$ with
$i + f(i) = \abs{w}$, and to the empty word when no such $i$ exists.
